decision: accepted one long-lived server owner with fresh mutable state for every request
why: this preserves safe reusable work without letting diagnostics, macros, typing progress, or target buffers leak into the next compile
result: architecture accepted; no readiness change

decision: made stdio and socket unification the first implementation slice
why: cache evidence is ambiguous while the two transports execute different compiler behavior
result: first child is deliberately cache-free

decision: kept existing semantic names and required deterministic cross-request revisions around them
why: current type and declaration IDs are useful names, while local body fingerprints and integer revisions do not identify all cache inputs
result: extend rather than replace existing identity work

decision: selected in-memory source/discovery/parse reuse before dependency observation and sealed typed-module reuse
why: this proves invalidation in smaller steps and avoids freezing an unproven persistent format
result: persistent typed cache deferred by evidence gate

decision: required fresh macro execution initially and worker isolation for changeable native plugins
why: macro effects are not fully observable yet and OCaml dynlink cannot safely unload a changed native module
result: no macro-result cache or main-process plugin reload

decision: set TypeScript and Go style edit loops as measured comparison baselines rather than cache-hit marketing
why: users experience total edit-to-result time, including target generation and Dune compilation, not an internal hit counter
result: competitive or better is a benchmark goal, not a current claim

decision: kept the current compilation-server guide truthful and made route-specific docs and tested examples a shipping gate
why: users need defaults, setup, ownership, reset, security, limitations, and troubleshooting before server use becomes normal
result: comprehensive current guide exists; native quickstarts follow implemented slices

decision: left README and North Star percentages unchanged
why: the review selects an implementation path but does not deliver safe native incremental compilation
result: progress bars unchanged

decision: separated effective upstream-Haxe Reflaxe reuse from the native hxhx server
why: upstream Haxe already owns a real compiler cache while native hxhx must build one; both need the same complete target-state and output-ownership principles
result: two connected products with separate host cache owners

decision: identified Haxe onGenerate as the complete public generation view and onAfterTyping as an incremental batch callback
why: Haxe passes all current generated types to onGenerate, while Reflaxe currently replaces its stored program with the latest after-typing batch
result: framework adapter must normalize the complete generation view

decision: moved request decoding and compile-or-display selection into one Haxe-owned dispatcher used by stdio and socket transports
why: the OCaml socket bridge previously made compiler decisions and rejected ordinary compilation, which created a second behavior path
result: first cache-free transport seam implemented; native snapshot regeneration and runtime equivalence still required

decision: added a focused interpreter test for immutable decoded requests, shared compile dispatch, display dispatch, and socket error framing
why: the lowest-cost test should prove the new ownership boundary before expensive bootstrap regeneration
result: focused source contract passes

decision: treated the first 900-second bootstrap emit cutoff as a tooling failure rather than native callback evidence
why: the process remained CPU-active and left no completed snapshot, so success or failure of the callback boundary could not be inferred
evidence: regenerate-hxhx-bootstrap.sh heartbeat: 900s cutoff, no leaked process, packages/hxhx/out returned to 32K
result: partial output stayed isolated; a smaller native boundary probe was required before retry

decision: proved a Haxe String-to-String function can be passed into and called by an OCaml extern
why: the socket design depends on the generated OCaml representation of a Haxe callback, and a tiny native program tests that dependency without rebuilding the whole compiler
evidence: .tmp/native-callback-probe generated and built with reflaxe.ocaml; runtime output haxe:request
result: callback representation is viable

decision: regenerated and built the native hxhx snapshot with the Haxe-owned callback dispatcher
why: the committed native compiler must match its Haxe source and compile the callback across the real runtime bridge
evidence: bootstrap regeneration 662s; build-hxhx.sh passed; generated HxHxCompilerServer.waitSocket mode handleRequest call inspected
result: native snapshot is source-aligned

decision: added and passed an ordinary socket compile beside the existing display roundtrip
why: the old socket bridge rejected ordinary compilation, so success must include a real generated artifact and runtime behavior rather than an OK-shaped reply
evidence: scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh with prebuilt native hxhx: display request passed, SocketCompileMain generated JavaScript printed socket-compile-ok, full lane passed in 838s
result: first transport-ownership sub-slice is green; request output capture and lifecycle remain

decision: left README goal percentages unchanged after the transport sub-slice
why: socket ordinary compilation is useful but there is still no semantic reuse, client-scoped output capture, complete request lifecycle, or clean-warm proof
result: child remains open and native incremental compilation remains unsupported

decision: separated complete type-list capture at onGenerate from final body capture at onAfterGenerate
why: Haxe invokes onGenerate before DCE and post-DCE constructor and field-initializer rewrites; onGenerate is complete membership evidence but not the final-body seal
result: previous 05:09 wording is superseded; Reflaxe must copy final retained bodies at onAfterGenerate

decision: converted a thrown socket request handler into a deterministic Haxe error-control response
why: the transport previously swallowed the exception and returned no bytes, which the client could misread as success
result: native fork/socket fixture proves the error byte and original failure context

decision: accepted and addressed the fresh-agent review of the first transport slice
why: an independent reader found that the lifecycle wording placed final-body capture too early and that socket callback failures could be swallowed
evidence: fresh Codex subagent review; lifecycle checkpoint; native callback-failure fixture
result: both high-impact findings corrected; malformed frames, nonzero compiler results, and client-scoped diagnostics remain within the open child Bead

decision: gave every native compiler request its own ordered output owner and returned ordinary progress and diagnostics to the requesting client
why: process-wide printing lets one request leak into the server log or another client and makes failure isolation impossible to prove
result: direct commands preserve immediate output; server requests buffer copied events and reject writes after closure

decision: proved native socket success to failure to success with client-scoped output and a silent server process
why: a unit-level reply is insufficient evidence that generated native code and the public connect client preserve protocol behavior
result: both successful requests generated runnable JavaScript; missing-main diagnostics reached only the failing client; no compiler output leaked to server stdout or stderr
